exercise.name: Dumbbell Iron Cross
aliases: Dumbbell T raise from the front

reference.title: Dumbbell Iron Cross
reference.listing: Video; the page could not be read here (blocked), so the movement follows the name and standard coaching (dumbbells together in front, quarter squat, rise and sweep out to a T).

exercise.mechanics: Compound (horizontal shoulder abduction at shoulder height with a quarter squat)

breathing.pattern: Inhale in the quarter squat; exhale as you stand and open the arms; inhale as they come back together.
breathing.cadence: About 1.4 s up, a short hold, about 1.8 s down

prescription.tempo: Controlled: about 1.5 s up and out, 0.5 s hold, 2 s back
prescription.load: User-chosen light dumbbells: long arms at shoulder height make even light weights hard
prescription.progression: Longer holds in the T, then heavier dumbbells

cues.text: Feet hip width, quarter squat; dumbbells together in front at shoulder height, arms long, thumbs up.
Stand up as both arms sweep out to the sides at shoulder height.
Hold the T: arms level with the shoulders, shoulder blades back, no shrug, no lean back.
Bring the dumbbells back together in front as you sink into the quarter squat.
Arms still at shoulder height; brace and go again.

mistakes.mistake: Arms drifting above or below shoulder height
mistakes.fix: Keep the hands level with the shoulders the whole time; go lighter.
Shoulders down and back; think long neck.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning back to get the arms out
mistakes.fix: Ribs down, trunk still; the legs drive, the arms sweep.
Keep a soft bend in the elbows.

kinematics.norm: Quarter squat: about 40-45 degrees of knee bend, rising to standing (standard coaching; clinical opinion)
From straight ahead with the dumbbells together to a T in line with the shoulders; rear-deltoid work in horizontal abduction (Schoenfeld 2013)
About shoulder height throughout; lateral and front deltoid hold the arm up (Campos 2020)

sources.title: GymVisual #5042, Dumbbell Iron Cross, video (movement reference)
Schoenfeld et al. 2013, effect of hand position on EMG activity of the posterior shoulder musculature during a horizontal abduction exercise (J Strength Cond Res 27(10):2644-2649)
Campos et al. 2020, different shoulder exercises affect the activation of deltoid portions in resistance-trained individuals (J Hum Kinet 75:5-14)
Coratella et al. 2020, an electromyographic analysis of lateral raise variations and frontal raise in competitive bodybuilders (Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(17):6015)

cautions: Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Shoulder pain or impingement symptoms: lower the arms below shoulder height or use no weight.
Choose light dumbbells; the long lever multiplies the load at the shoulder.
Low-back pain: keep the ribs down and avoid leaning back.
modify: No squat: stand still and do only the arm sweep.
Bent elbows (90 degrees) to shorten the lever.
progressions: Hold the T for 3-5 s each rep.

muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Posterior deltoid drives the horizontal sweep out to the T; it is most active in horizontal abduction (Schoenfeld 2013).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Posterior deltoid drives the horizontal sweep out to the T; it is most active in horizontal abduction (Schoenfeld 2013).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Middle deltoid holds the arms at shoulder height and helps the sweep (Campos 2020; Coratella 2020).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_l: Middle deltoid holds the arms at shoulder height and helps the sweep (Campos 2020; Coratella 2020).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Pull the shoulder blades back as the arms open (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Pull the shoulder blades back as the arms open (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Rotator cuff steadies the shoulder through the sweep (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Rotator cuff steadies the shoulder through the sweep (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Holds the arms up in front at the start (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Holds the arms up in front at the start (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_r: Drive the rise out of the quarter squat (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Drive the rise out of the quarter squat (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Extends the hips on the way up (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Extends the hips on the way up (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Supports the shoulder girdle; should not shrug (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Supports the shoulder girdle; should not shrug (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Keeps the shoulder blades on the ribs (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Keeps the shoulder blades on the ribs (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the trunk upright in the squat (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the trunk upright in the squat (clinical opinion).
